PRE-00.title: PRE-00 — Canary
PRE-00.objective:
Exercise the **identical** measurement path — quiesce, drop_caches, thermal pre-check, rails, fio, parse,
rails reconcile, cache-lie gate, physical ceiling gate — end to end, at the lowest cost that can prove the
path is intact, immediately after preconditioning and before the first real case is measured. Physical
question: is the whole instrumented pipeline actually working on this pool/layout, right now? Nothing a
NAS buyer reads directly; this is the cell's own self-test, not a reported performance number (imperative
case: a broken path must fail ~15 s after preconditioning, not after the first 4.5-minute write case).
PRE-00.pass_fail:

- Cache-lie gate: physical read rate >= 50% of logical read rate (logical read on the preconditioned
- Steadiness record is written (read-class rule, README §7) but is informational here: PRE-00 is far too
 short (10 s window) to be judged by the same convergence standard as the real read cases, and its
 `steady` value is not treated as a case-level pass/fail signal.

Identical hard-gate failure modes to every other case (README §10): fio nonzero exit or no output/log,
duration outside the 0.8x-1.5x band, physical read below the ceiling, or a cache-lie. Any of these aborts
purpose is to fail exactly like a real case would, just sooner and cheaper.

pool member and to heat-soak the DRAM-less NVMe controllers, ending on a steady-state detector under a
1-hour hard cap. Physical question: what does this layout do once the drives' write cache is spent and the
controllers have been running hot for tens of minutes — the thing a 90 s STO-01 case cannot show (protocol

import) that runs long enough to leave the drive's fast cache behind.

SOAK-02.title: SOAK-02 — Mixed Workload Soak
SOAK-02.objective:
70/30 read/write random 16k traffic against the 16K-volblock zvol, sustained for up to 30 minutes and
ending on a steady-state detector. Physical question: what does this layout's file-server-shaped mixed
traffic look like over a duration long enough for the pool's dirty-data and read paths to reach a genuine
steady state, as opposed to STO-03's 90 s snapshot of the same shape. NAS buyer: this is the multi-user
steady state sustained over the length of a real session, not a burst.

### Pass Criteria

- fio exits 0; accounted duration >= `0.95 * 900 = 855 s` (the `floor_seconds:` lower bound) and `<= 1.5 *
 1800 = 2700 s` (the usual upper bound against the `CAP` target).
- `max([rate], [rate]) <= [rate]` (`compressratio=1.0`) — per-direction, same as STO-03; the
 aggregate may exceed the ceiling on this mixed workload.
- Cache-lie gate: physical read rate >= 50% of logical read rate whenever logical read exceeds [redacted].

fio nonzero exit, duration-band violation, a ceiling violation on either direction, or a cache-lie on the

STO-02.title: STO-02 — Random IOPS Sweep
STO-02.objective:
Random read and write IOPS across three block sizes (4k, 16k, 64k) against a 16K-volblocksize zvol.
Physical question: how does this layout's random-access performance scale with request size, from
sub-volblock (4k, forces read-modify-write on writes) through block-aligned (16k) to multi-block (64k,
gathers/scatters across multiple volblocks). NAS buyer: this is the shape of database, VM-disk, and
many-small-client-connection traffic, not sequential transfer.
STO-02.pass_fail:
### Pass Criteria

Same hard gates as every case (README §§5-7), applied per sub-case:
- fio exits 0; accounted duration within 0.8x-1.5x of target (read 96-180 s, write 216-405 s).
- `max([rate], [rate]) <= [rate]` (`compressratio=1.0`, `bv16k` runs `compression=off`).
- Cache-lie gate on the three read sub-cases: physical read rate >= 50% of logical (scaled by
 compressratio) whenever logical read exceeds [redacted].
- Steadiness recorded per sub-case: read sub-cases by window SE, write sub-cases by physical trend +
 logical CV against this layout's own noise (README §7).
- `bv16k`'s property assertions and full preconditioning passed before STO-02 could run.

### Fail Criteria

Identical failure modes to STO-01 (README §10): fio nonzero exit, duration-band violation, ceiling

STO-03.title: STO-03 — Mixed Read/Write
STO-03.objective:
70% read / 30% write random traffic at 16k against the 16K-volblock zvol, 4 concurrent jobs. Physical
question: how does this layout behave under simultaneous contending read and write pressure at a
block-aligned size, as opposed to the pure-read or pure-write sub-cases of STO-02. NAS buyer: this is the
closest single case in the suite to an actual multi-user file-server steady state — read-heavy, but never
purely read.
STO-03.pass_fail:
### Pass Criteria

- fio exits 0; accounted duration within 0.8x-1.5x of 270 s (216-405 s).
- `max([rate], [rate]) <= [rate]` (`compressratio=1.0`) — the gate is per direction, so the
 70/30 mix's *aggregate* `[rate]` (read+write combined) may legitimately exceed `[rate]`; only
 `[rate]` and `[rate]` individually are asserted against it (README §6, link full duplex).
- Cache-lie gate: physical read rate >= 50% of logical read rate (scaled by compressratio) — applies here
 because the workload's read side exceeds [redacted] logical.
- Steadiness: write-class rule (physical trend + logical CV against this layout's own bucket noise).

### Fail Criteria

Same as every case (README §10): fio nonzero exit, duration-band violation, either direction's rate above
`[rate]`, or a cache-lie on the read side aborts the whole cell.

STO-04.title: STO-04 — Synchronous Write
STO-04.objective:
Random 16k writes with `--fsync=1` (an fsync after every write) against a small, fixed 8 GiB region.
Physical question: what latency and IOPS does this layout deliver when every write must be durably
committed before the next one issues — the thing sequential/buffered throughput numbers cannot show.
NAS buyer: this is the shape of database commits and VM-disk writes, where the caller waits on each write,
not a bulk-transfer number.
STO-04.pass_fail:
### Pass Criteria

- fio exits 0; accounted duration within 0.8x-1.5x of 270 s (216-405 s).
- `[rate] <= [rate]` (`compressratio=1.0`) — expected to be far below the ceiling: `fsync=1`
 serializes each write behind a durable commit, so this case is latency-bound, not link-bound (see
 Comments for the
- Steadiness: write-class rule (physical trend + logical CV against this layout's own bucket noise).
- No cache-lie gate applies in practice: this case's logical *read* rate is 0 (pure `randwrite`), so the
 read-side gate (which only fires when logical read exceeds [redacted]) does not trigger.

### Fail Criteria

Same as every case (README §10): fio nonzero exit or duration-band violation aborts the whole cell. A
ceiling violation here would be unusual given the workload's latency-bound nature, but the gate is
unconditional and still applies.

STO-05.title: STO-05 — RAIDZ Padding Penalty
STO-05.objective:
The identical 64k random write workload run against two zvols that differ in exactly one property:
`volblocksize` (16K vs 64K). Physical question: how much does volblocksize alone cost or save on a
raidz-family layout, isolated from every other variable (target, working set, job count, block size are
all held constant). NAS buyer: this is the number that answers "should I set a bigger volblock/recordsize
for large-file workloads on this array," independent of which redundancy scheme is chosen.
STO-05.pass_fail:
### Pass Criteria

Per sub-case, same hard gates as every write case (README §§5-7):
- fio exits 0; accounted duration within 0.8x-1.5x of 270 s (216-405 s).
- `[rate] <= [rate]` (`compressratio=1.0`).
- Steadiness: write-class rule (physical trend + logical CV against this layout's own bucket noise),
 recorded independently per sub-case.
- No read-side cache-lie gate applies (pure `randwrite`, logical read = 0).

### Fail Criteria

Same as every case (README §10): fio nonzero exit, duration-band violation, or a ceiling violation in
either sub-case aborts the whole cell.

Physical question: how does this layout's random-access performance scale with request size, from
sub-volblock (4k, forces read-modify-write on writes) through block-aligned (16k) to multi-block (64k,
gathers/scatters across multiple volblocks). NAS buyer: this is the shape of database, VM-disk, and
many-small-client-connection traffic, not sequential transfer.
STO-02_rand_read_4k_j4.pass_fail:
### Pass Criteria

Same hard gates as every case (README §§5-7), applied per sub-case:
- fio exits 0; accounted duration within 0.8x-1.5x of target (read 96-180 s, write 216-405 s).
- `max([rate], [rate]) <= [rate]` (`compressratio=1.0`, `bv16k` runs `compression=off`).
- Cache-lie gate on the three read sub-cases: physical read rate >= 50% of logical (scaled by
 compressratio) whenever logical read exceeds [redacted].
- Steadiness recorded per sub-case: read sub-cases by window SE, write sub-cases by physical trend +
 logical CV against this layout's own noise (README §7).
- `bv16k`'s property assertions and full preconditioning passed before STO-02 could run.

### Fail Criteria

Identical failure modes to STO-01 (README §10): fio nonzero exit, duration-band violation, ceiling

STO-03_mixed_70r30w_16k_j4.title: STO-03 — Mixed Read/Write
STO-03_mixed_70r30w_16k_j4.objective:
70% read / 30% write random traffic at 16k against the 16K-volblock zvol, 4 concurrent jobs. Physical
question: how does this layout behave under simultaneous contending read and write pressure at a
block-aligned size, as opposed to the pure-read or pure-write sub-cases of STO-02. NAS buyer: this is the
closest single case in the suite to an actual multi-user file-server steady state — read-heavy, but never
purely read.
STO-03_mixed_70r30w_16k_j4.pass_fail:
### Pass Criteria

- fio exits 0; accounted duration within 0.8x-1.5x of 270 s (216-405 s).
- `max([rate], [rate]) <= [rate]` (`compressratio=1.0`) — the gate is per direction, so the
 70/30 mix's *aggregate* `[rate]` (read+write combined) may legitimately exceed `[rate]`; only
 `[rate]` and `[rate]` individually are asserted against it (README §6, link full duplex).
- Cache-lie gate: physical read rate >= 50% of logical read rate (scaled by compressratio) — applies here
 because the workload's read side exceeds [redacted] logical.
- Steadiness: write-class rule (physical trend + logical CV against this layout's own bucket noise).

### Fail Criteria

Same as every case (README §10): fio nonzero exit, duration-band violation, either direction's rate above
`[rate]`, or a cache-lie on the read side aborts the whole cell.

STO-04_sync_write_16k_j4.title: STO-04 — Synchronous Write
STO-04_sync_write_16k_j4.objective:
Random 16k writes with `--fsync=1` (an fsync after every write) against a small, fixed 8 GiB region.
Physical question: what latency and IOPS does this layout deliver when every write must be durably
committed before the next one issues — the thing sequential/buffered throughput numbers cannot show.
NAS buyer: this is the shape of database commits and VM-disk writes, where the caller waits on each write,
not a bulk-transfer number.
STO-04_sync_write_16k_j4.pass_fail:
### Pass Criteria

- fio exits 0; accounted duration within 0.8x-1.5x of 270 s (216-405 s).
- `[rate] <= [rate]` (`compressratio=1.0`) — expected to be far below the ceiling: `fsync=1`
 serializes each write behind a durable commit, so this case is latency-bound, not link-bound (see
 Comments for the
- Steadiness: write-class rule (physical trend + logical CV against this layout's own bucket noise).
- No cache-lie gate applies in practice: this case's logical *read* rate is 0 (pure `randwrite`), so the
 read-side gate (which only fires when logical read exceeds [redacted]) does not trigger.

### Fail Criteria

Same as every case (README §10): fio nonzero exit or duration-band violation aborts the whole cell. A
ceiling violation here would be unusual given the workload's latency-bound nature, but the gate is
unconditional and still applies.

STO-05_rand_write_64k_vbs16k_j4.title: STO-05 — RAIDZ Padding Penalty
STO-05_rand_write_64k_vbs16k_j4.objective:
The identical 64k random write workload run against two zvols that differ in exactly one property:
`volblocksize` (16K vs 64K). Physical question: how much does volblocksize alone cost or save on a
raidz-family layout, isolated from every other variable (target, working set, job count, block size are
all held constant). NAS buyer: this is the number that answers "should I set a bigger volblock/recordsize
for large-file workloads on this array," independent of which redundancy scheme is chosen.
STO-05_rand_write_64k_vbs16k_j4.pass_fail:
### Pass Criteria

Per sub-case, same hard gates as every write case (README §§5-7):
- fio exits 0; accounted duration within 0.8x-1.5x of 270 s (216-405 s).
- `[rate] <= [rate]` (`compressratio=1.0`).
- Steadiness: write-class rule (physical trend + logical CV against this layout's own bucket noise),
 recorded independently per sub-case.
- No read-side cache-lie gate applies (pure `randwrite`, logical read = 0).

### Fail Criteria

Same as every case (README §10): fio nonzero exit, duration-band violation, or a ceiling violation in
either sub-case aborts the whole cell.

STO-06_smallfiles_copy_1stream.title: STO-06 — Small Files

Copy, cache-dropped read-back, and delete of a 32,768-file corpus, single stream — the `cp`/`rsync` path,
not fio. Physical question: what does this layout actually deliver for the create-many-small-files,
read-them-back, and clean-up-afterward workload, including directory and dnode metadata cost and the
dataset's own compression. NAS buyer: sequential-1M and random-16k numbers do not describe a
photos/documents/source-tree share; this case does.

case states fio's `nrfiles`+`randwrite` approach measured small random I/O over *pre-existing* files, not
the small-file create/open/close path a real copy exercises — STO-06 exists to measure the thing fio's own
job model cannot.

- Cache-lie gate on the read phase: physical read rate >= 50% of logical read rate scaled by the measured
 compressratio, whenever logical read exceeds [redacted].

 (README §7) — never a gate, because there is no 1 s logical series for a shell command to compute a
